proposed_fix.description: Investigate checkoutservice's node/pod network for added latency, and only after confirming a cause, move the checkoutservice pod to another node as a reversible mitigation.
steps: Identify the node and pod hosting checkoutservice and compare its network latency (ping/tcp connect time) to the 6 callees against a pod on a different node.
Check for network-level delay on the pod/node: tc qdisc rules (netem), CNI/NetworkPolicy changes, or a sidecar/proxy introducing latency.
Check node network and conntrack health (interface drops, conntrack count vs limit) to confirm or rule out R3 as the cause before any change.
If the node is implicated, cordon it and request human approval to reschedule the checkoutservice pod to a different node (rolling restart, one replica at a time).
After the move, verify checkoutservice latency-50/90 and outbound span self-time return toward baseline (~3-4ms p50).
preconditions: Confirm checkoutservice has more than one replica or tolerates a rolling restart without dropping checkouts.
Confirm other nodes have spare cpu/memory capacity to host the pod.
Confirm no recent deploy or network policy change on checkoutservice that could be rolled back more simply.
Human on-call approves any cordon or reschedule action.
proposed_fix.rollback: Uncordon the node and reschedule or scale the checkoutservice pod back to its original placement; revert any tc/NetworkPolicy change to its prior saved state.

contradictions.why: Errors are 0.0->0.0 and the delay hits only checkoutservice's own outbound calls to all callees, which does not indicate a physical link fault, so hardware replacement is not supported and is excluded.

contradictions.step: Bump conntrack limit directly on the node, remembering to make it persistent across node reboots.
contradictions.why: There is no evidence of conntrack exhaustion (zero errors, only added latency), so a persistent node-level limit change is unsupported and excluded; only the read-only check is kept.
